Docs/Shipready/Saves

Shipready: API Reference

Version 1.0.0 · Rare Geometry · Generated 2026-10-30

Every public type and member of Shipready, generated from the documentation comments in its source code. 191 types and 2091 members in 25 namespaces.

For explanations, walkthroughs and examples, start with the Guide; for how each part works, the Reference. Every error code has an entry in Troubleshooting.

Assembly What it holds Runs in
RareGeometry.Shipready.Save Saving and loading, slots, files, backups, compression and encryption, world persistence, migrations and the co-op hooks Game and Editor
RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI The save and load menu, its theme and text assets, thumbnails and test hotkeys Game and Editor
RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Core The core editor services, which need no UI package: saved ids for Saveables, registry upkeep, loading saved scenes outside Build Settings in the Editor, and the migration link file for builds Editor only, never in a build
RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor The Setup Wizard, Save Inspector, Diagnostics, the Saveable inspector and Field Picker, and the generators. Needs uGUI and TextMesh Pro Editor only, never in a build
RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Setup Install Required Packages, which installs uGUI and TextMesh Pro in a project that lacks them, and stops a player build until they are in. It compiles only while one of them is missing Editor only, never in a build

How to read this reference:

  • Most game code needs only using RareGeometry.Shipready.Save;. A type in another namespace shows its namespace under its name.
  • Signatures are C# as declared, including default values. Members are listed by name; enum values in declaration order. Inherited members are not repeated.
  • Calls that can fail return a result (SaveResult or LoadResult) with an error code, a plain-English message and a link to Troubleshooting. They do not throw.

  • SaveEvents · static class. The points a game can hook into: a save or load starting, finishing, or finishing by falling back to a backup.

AnimatorSaver #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class AnimatorSaver : MonoBehaviour, ISaveable

The Animator saver: an Animator's parameters (floats, ints and bools), and for each layer the state it is in, how far through it is, and the layer's weight. Add it beside a Saveable; no code. A door saved half open comes back half open, a character saved crouching comes back crouching.

Triggers are not saved: they last one moment and would fire again on load. A layer in the middle of a blend is saved as the state it is blending into. The state comes back once the Animator is ready, on its first frame after the load, so an object loaded inactive takes it when it is switched on.

Add Component menu: Shipready → Savers → Animator Saver

AudioSourceSaver #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class AudioSourceSaver : MonoBehaviour, ISaveable

The Audio Source saver: whether an AudioSource is playing, how far into its clip it is, and its volume and pitch. Add it beside a Saveable; no code. Music saved halfway through comes back halfway through, a radio switched off stays off.

The clip itself is not changed: the AudioSource keeps the clip it has in the scene. The state comes back as soon as the AudioSource can play, so an object loaded inactive takes it when it is switched on.

AutosaveScheduler #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class AutosaveScheduler

Decides when an autosave is due. Each trigger is optional, and the Setup Wizard asks which ones a game wants.

The timer counts in unscaled time, so pausing the game by setting the time scale to zero does not stop autosaves, and it restarts after every autosave rather than drifting.

EnabledSaver #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class EnabledSaver : MonoBehaviour, ISaveable

The Enabled saver: the enabled tick box of the components you choose, such as a light, a renderer, a collider or one of your scripts. Add it beside a Saveable and drag the components into its list; no code. A lamp switched off stays off, a trap disarmed by switching off its collider stays disarmed.

Any component with an enabled tick box works: every Behaviour (scripts, lights, audio sources, UI), every Renderer and every Collider. When it is added, the list starts with the ones on this object. The order of the list is how the saved values are matched, so add new components at the end in a game update.

ISaveable #

interface in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public interface ISaveable

Implemented by a component that writes and reads its own state. This is the way out for anything the built-in savers and the Field Picker cannot cover: dictionaries, polymorphic data, properties, or a value that has to be worked out rather than copied.

Shipready calls CaptureState(SaveWriter) on the main thread while a save is being gathered, and RestoreState(SaveReader) after Unity has woken the scene and before Start runs, so code in Start already sees the saved values. Set defaults in Awake or in field initialisers, never in Start.

Example

public class Chest : MonoBehaviour, ISaveable
{
    [SerializeField] bool isOpen;

    public void CaptureState(SaveWriter w) { w.Write("open", isOpen); }
    public void RestoreState(SaveReader r) { isOpen = r.Read("open", false); }
}

NavMeshAgentSaver #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class NavMeshAgentSaver : MonoBehaviour, ISaveable

The NavMesh Agent saver: where a NavMeshAgent is, where it was walking to, its speed and whether it was stopped. Add it beside a Saveable; no code. A guard saved on patrol carries on to the same point after a load.

The agent is moved with Warp, which a NavMeshAgent needs: moving its transform alone would be undone by the agent. That happens on the agent's first frame after the load, after the Saveable has put the transform back, so leave the Saveable's Position saver on or off as you like. An agent that is not on a NavMesh at that moment keeps its position and only takes the speed.

Saveable #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class Saveable : MonoBehaviour, ISerializationCallbackReceiver

Makes a GameObject part of the saved world. Add it to an object and the object's position, active state and the fields ticked in its Field Picker come back on load, matched by a permanent id. Scripts on the same object that implement ISaveable are saved with it.

The built-in savers: Position (local position, rotation, scale and parent), Active, Destroyed (an object destroyed during play stays destroyed, or disabled) and Physics (velocities and sleep state of a Rigidbody or Rigidbody2D; switched on automatically when the object has one).

Ids are automatic. An object placed in a scene gets one in the Editor, and a copy gets a new one. An object spawned from a prefab at runtime gets a runtime id and is saved with its prefab id, so a load can re-create it.

Add Component menu: Shipready → Saveable

Properties

Category
public string Category { get; set; }

The category this object is saved in. Left empty in the Inspector it is the world category from the settings, normally World; setting an empty value goes back to that.

What a remembered destruction does when the scene comes back: destroy or disable.

The permanent id this object is saved under. Scene objects carry the id they were given in the Editor; runtime objects get one when they wake up. Empty on a prefab asset and on an object that never woke up.

IsRuntimeSpawned

Whether this object was made at runtime, by spawning a prefab or copying another object, rather than placed in a scene. A load re-creates runtime objects from their prefab.

The id of the prefab this object was made from: the prefab asset's GUID, set by the Editor. Empty for an object that is not part of a prefab.

Whether the active state is saved. On by default.

Whether destroying this object during play is remembered, so it stays destroyed after a load or when its scene comes back. On by default. Unloading a scene or quitting never counts as destroying.

Whether the velocities and sleep state of a Rigidbody or Rigidbody2D are saved. Restored bodies are held still until the next physics step, so objects that touch do not push each other apart.

Whether the local position, rotation, scale and parent are saved. On by default.

SaveActions #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveActions : MonoBehaviour

Saving and loading without code: drop this on any object, then pick one of its methods in a UI Button's On Click list (or any UnityEvent): Save To Slot, Load Slot, Quicksave, Quickload, Autosave, Continue, New Game, Delete Slot or Delete All Saves. The slot number goes in the box beside the method.

Each call runs in the background, so the game does not stop while a file is written, and then raises OnSucceeded or OnFailed, for a sound or a message. A call made while another is still running waits its turn in Shipready, as any save does. Nothing here asks the player first: put a confirmation in front of Delete in your own UI, or use the save menu, which asks.

Add Component menu: Shipready → Save Actions

SaveData #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveData

The plain values a game saves: gold, the current day, a volume setting, a list of unlocked levels. One line to store a value and one to read it back.

Values live in memory until a save writes them, and a load replaces them. Every value belongs to a category, which decides whether it ends up inside a slot or in the one global file that a slot load never touches.

Example

SaveKit.Data.Set("gold", gold, "Progress");
gold = SaveKit.Data.Get("gold", 0);

Properties

CategoryCount
public int CategoryCount { get; }

How many categories hold at least one value.

DefaultCategory
public string DefaultCategory { get; }

The category a value goes into when the game does not name one.

Methods

Clear()
public void Clear();

Forgets every value in every category, which is what starting a new game wants. Nothing on disk is touched.

A save only replaces the categories that hold values. A category with nothing in it keeps whatever the file being saved over already holds, which is what stops a save from wiping player settings that were never loaded. To start a slot afresh, delete it with SaveKit.Delete(int) before saving into it.

SaveErrorCode #

enum in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public enum SaveErrorCode

Every outcome Shipready can report. Each value has a stable SK identifier and one entry in Documentation/Troubleshooting.md, so a message in the Console always leads to a fix. Values are grouped by hundreds and are never renumbered, because saved support reports quote them.

Values

Name Value Description
None 0 The call succeeded and there is nothing to report. SK000.
Unknown 1 Something failed that Shipready could not classify. SK001.
InvalidArgument 2 A value handed to Shipready was missing, empty or out of range. SK002.
Busy 3 Another save or load is already running for this file and did not finish in time. SK003.

Reserved for custom storage: Shipready itself never returns it in 1.0, because saves and loads of one file wait in a queue and run in order. A custom ISaveStorage may return it from a call it could not get access for.
Cancelled 4 The call was cancelled before it finished. SK004.

Reserved for custom storage: the 1.0 API has no way to cancel a call, so Shipready itself never returns it. A custom ISaveStorage may return it from a call that was stopped. A kit stopped or restarted during a call reports NotInitialised instead.
NotInitialised 5 Shipready was used before it was initialised, usually a missing settings asset. SK005.
FileNotFound 100 No file exists for that slot or name. SK100.
FileDamaged 101 The file could not be read as a save at all, and no valid copy was found. SK101.
RecoveredFromBackup 102 The main file was unusable, so a backup was loaded instead. The load succeeded. SK102.
UnsupportedFormat 103 The file is a save, but in an envelope format Shipready version cannot read. SK103.
ChecksumMismatch 104 The checksum does not match the data, so the file was changed or truncated. SK104.
TamperDetected 105 An encrypted file failed its tamper check. SK105.
EncryptionKeyWrong 106 An encrypted file could not be decrypted with the current passphrase. SK106.
CompressionFailed 107 Compressed data could not be unpacked. SK107.
DiskFull 110 The disk has no room left. Existing saves were not touched. SK110.
AccessDenied 111 The folder or file could not be written, usually a permission or read-only problem. SK111.
StorageUnavailable 112 The storage layer could not be reached, for example a removed drive. SK112.
PathTooLong 113 The resulting file path is longer than the platform allows. SK113.
NewerVersion 120 The file was written by a newer save version than this build understands. SK120.
MigrationMissing 121 A migration step needed to upgrade this file does not exist. SK121.
MigrationFailed 122 A migration step ran but failed. SK122.
SaveVersionInvalid 123 The configured save version is not a valid whole number above zero. SK123.
ObjectNotFound 130 A saved object no longer exists in the scene, so its state was skipped. SK130.
PrefabNotRegistered 131 A saved runtime object names a prefab that is not in the Prefab Registry. SK131.
AssetNotRegistered 132 A saved reference names an asset that is not in the Asset Registry. SK132.
SceneNotRegistered 133 A saved scene is not in the Scene Registry. SK133.
SceneNotInBuildSettings 134 A scene the save needs is not in Build Settings, so it cannot be loaded. SK134.
HostOnly 140 Only the host or a solo player may do this. SK140.
PlayerUnknown 141 A connected player could not be matched to a stable player id, so they start from defaults. SK141. Reported in the Console by SaveKit.Players.ForConnection and SaveKit.Players.TryGetPlayerId when the game's IPlayerIdentity fails, and by ForConnection when no identity is set or the identity does not name the connection. A player id the save has never seen is not this code: that player simply gets empty data.
CategoryUnknown 150 A category name was used that the settings asset does not define. SK150.
SlotOutOfRange 151 The slot number is outside the configured range. SK151.
SlotEmpty 152 The slot holds no save yet. SK152.
SettingsInvalid 153 A value in the settings asset cannot be used, such as a file name pattern without {0} in it. SK153.
LoadInProgress 154 A load is still loading the scenes its save was made in, so a save now would write a half-restored world over what the load just put back. Nothing was written. Save again once the load has finished. SK154.

SaveEvents #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class SaveEvents

The points a game can hook into: a save or load starting, finishing, or finishing by falling back to a backup.

A handler runs on the main thread, so it is safe to touch Unity objects, show a saving icon or pause the game from one. The one thing a handler must not do is start another save of the same file, which would queue behind the one that is finishing.

Handlers are cleared when static state resets, so turning off domain reload cannot leave a handler from a previous play session attached to a destroyed object.

Properties

Generation
public static int Generation { get; }

Changes every time the handlers are cleared, which SaveKit.Shutdown() does. A component that listens for as long as it lives compares it with the number it subscribed under, and subscribes again when it changed, so it keeps working after Shipready is stopped and started again (a profile switch, for example).

Removes every handler. Called when static state resets.

Raised when a load starts, before the file is read.

Saved

Raised when a save has finished, successfully or not.

Saving

Raised when a save starts, before anything is gathered. A handler can still put its latest values into SaveKit.Data here and they are part of the save. Values changed after the save call returns are not, because the save works on a copy.

SaveKit #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class SaveKit

The front door. Everything a game needs for saving is reachable from here: the plain values, the slots, the global file, the autosaves and the migrations.

Nothing here throws. Every call hands back a result with a code, a plain-English message and a link into the Troubleshooting guide.

Every call that ends in Async finishes back on the main thread, so the code after an await can touch Unity objects freely. That also means the main thread must be left free to get there: never call .Wait() or read .Result on one of these tasks from the main thread, because the task is waiting for that same thread and the game would stop dead. When a save has to finish before the next line runs, which is the case when the game is quitting, use the plain Save(int, string[]) and Load(int, string[]) instead. They are built for exactly that.

A save only gathers the values on the main thread. Reading the file already there, bringing it up to date, merging, packing and writing all happen on a background thread, in the queue for that file. A load reads, checks and migrates on a background thread and only puts the values into Data back on the main thread.

Example

SaveKit.Data.Set("gold", gold, "Progress");
SaveResult saved = await SaveKit.SaveAsync(slot: 1);
if (!saved.Success) Debug.LogWarning(saved.Message);

Properties

Authority
public static ISaveAuthority Authority { get; set; }

Decides who may save and load world data. Null, the default, is a solo game: always allowed. When it says no, every slot, autosave and quicksave save, load and delete returns SaveErrorCode.HostOnly without touching storage; the global file stays available, so a co-op client keeps its own settings.

The plain values a game saves. Never null.

HasUnsavedProgress

Whether quitting now would lose play: the playtime (Playtime) has grown by at least UnsavedProgressSeconds since the progress was last safe on disk. Playtime stops while it is paused (the save menu and the Game Menu pause it while they are open), so time on a title screen or in a pause menu does not count. False before Shipready starts. The save menu's quit confirmation asks this.

Maps a connected player to the stable id their data is kept under. Null until a game sets one.

Whether Shipready has settings and somewhere to save to.

Where the player is, as the game wants it described on the slot card.

Migrations

The migration steps that bring old saves up to date. A game can add steps here instead of marking methods with [SaveMigration]. A step added here always wins over one found by its attribute, whether it is added before or after Shipready starts. Never null.

Per-player data in a co-op game, saved inside the host's slot under each player's stable id. Never null.

How long the player has played. Never null.

ProfileId
public static string ProfileId { get; set; }

Whose saves to use on a shared machine, such as the player's Steam ID. Set it before Initialise(SaveKitSettings): Shipready then replaces {profile} in SaveKitSettings.ProfileFolder with it, so a profile folder of {profile} keeps each player's saves in Saves/<id>. A profile folder without {profile} is used as it is, and then this id is not needed.

Changing it while Shipready runs does nothing until Shipready starts again. With {profile} in the profile folder and no id, Initialise fails with SaveErrorCode.SettingsInvalid rather than mixing players' saves, so switch off SaveKitSettings.InitialiseAutomatically and start Shipready yourself once the id is known. The id is kept by Shutdown(), so starting again uses it, and forgotten when a new play session starts. Null is stored as empty.

Example

SaveKit.ProfileId = SteamUser.GetSteamID().ToString();   // your Steam library's call
SaveKit.Initialise();

How long the game has been running since its progress was last safe on disk: the last slot save, autosave or quicksave that succeeded (counted from when its values were gathered), the last load, NewGame(), or Shipready starting, whichever came last. NewGame()
public static void NewGame();

Starts a new game in Shipready's data: every slot category becomes empty, so the next save replaces those categories in the file instead of keeping the old slot's; scene memory, destroyed lists, spawned objects and players are forgotten; the slot name, location, summary and playtime start again. Global categories, such as the player's settings, are kept. Nothing on disk is touched.

Shipready resets its data; the game resets its own scene objects. Either load the first scene of the new game straight after this (for example with LoadScene(string, LoadSceneMode)), or, to start the new game in the scene that is open, put that scene's objects back to their starting state yourself. Objects in the open scenes keep whatever state they have, and the next save captures them as they are.

The scenes open at this moment are marked, so that leaving them through LoadScene(string, LoadSceneMode) or UnloadScene(Scene) (or SaveWorld.CaptureScene(Scene) before an unload of your own) does not capture the old game back into scene memory. A save the player or your code asks for (Save(int, string[]), SaveAsync(int, string[]), SaveInBackground(int, Action<SaveResult>, string[]), a quicksave, or your own call to Autosave() or AutosaveAsync()) captures every loaded scene and clears the mark of each scene it captures, because from then on its state belongs to the new game. Shipready's own automatic saves (the timer, a scene change, quitting or being suspended) leave a marked scene out and keep its mark, so they can never write the old game's objects into the new game's save. Scenes loaded from now on are captured as usual.

RestoreBackup(int)
public static SaveResult RestoreBackup(int slot);

Puts the newest valid backup of a damaged slot back in place, and waits for it to finish. The menu offers this as Restore backup when automatic fallback is switched off (SaveFileOptions.AutomaticFallback).

The backup is copied unchanged over the main file through the crash-safe write, so the slot then loads normally and carries the backup's save time. The damaged main file is kept aside as .corrupt-<time>; the backups stay where they are. A main file that reads correctly is never replaced. Like Delete(int), a co-op client gets SaveErrorCode.HostOnly.

Parameter Description
slot The slot number, counting from 1.

Returns: SaveErrorCode.RecoveredFromBackup on success, which counts as a success; SaveErrorCode.FileDamaged when no backup is valid, with nothing changed.

SaveInBackground(int, Action<SaveResult>, string[])
public static void SaveInBackground(int slot, Action<SaveResult> onComplete, string[] categories = null);

Saves a slot on a background thread, as SaveAsync(int, string[]) does, and calls onComplete with the result when it has finished, for code that would rather not use await.

The callback runs on the main thread, so it can touch Unity objects. A save refused straight away, such as one to a slot out of range, calls it before this method returns. An exception thrown by the callback is caught and written to the Console; it never reaches Shipready or the game.

Parameter Description
slot The slot number, counting from 1.
onComplete What to call with the result. Null saves without telling anybody.
categories Which categories to save. Null saves all of them.

Example

SaveKit.SaveInBackground(1, result =>
{
    if (!result.Success) Debug.LogWarning(result.Message);
});

SetNextThumbnail(Texture2D)
public static void SetNextThumbnail(Texture2D texture);

Sets the picture the next slot save, autosave or quicksave stores beside its file, for the menu to show on the slot card. The picture is scaled down and copied straight away, so the game can destroy its texture as soon as this returns.

The picture is written after the save itself is safely in place, and is used once: the next successful save takes it and clears it. A picture that cannot be used, or cannot be written, is reported as a warning in that save's report and never fails the save. Call this on the main thread.

A successful slot save, autosave or quicksave made without a picture removes the thumbnail of the save it replaced, so a slot card never shows a picture of an older save. Slot saves, autosaves and quicksaves take their own picture while SaveKitSettings.CaptureAutosaveThumbnails is on, unless one was set here.

Parameter Description
texture The picture, usually from ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshotAsTexture. It has to be readable. Null clears a picture set earlier.

SetSummary(string[])
public static void SetSummary(params string[] lines);

Sets the short lines the slot card shows under the location, such as Day 12 and $4,300. Up to four are kept.

Parameter Description
lines The lines to show. Null or empty clears them.

Shutdown()
public static void Shutdown();

Stops Shipready and forgets its settings, storage, migrations, live values, event handlers, scene memory, players and co-op hooks (Authority, Identity, SpawnHandler and the scene loader). Nothing on disk is touched apart from the slot cache, which is written if it changed. A save or load still running finishes with SaveErrorCode.NotInitialised and changes nothing in memory.

Returns: The unload in progress, or null when the scene cannot be unloaded (reported in the Console).

SaveKitEnvironment #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class SaveKitEnvironment

The handful of Unity values Shipready needs while it is working on a background thread.

Unity only allows most of its API on the main thread, and the whole point of saving in the background is that the packing and the disk work happen off it. So the values are read once, on the main thread, and the background work reads the copies.

They are captured again whenever static state resets, so turning off domain reload cannot leave the previous play session values behind.

SaveKitRunner #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveKitRunner : MonoBehaviour

The one hidden object Shipready keeps in a running game. It counts playtime, watches the autosave timer, makes sure a save still happens when the game is closing, applies scene memory as scenes load, and lets go of restored rigidbodies on the next physics step.

It is created whenever Shipready starts in a running game, whichever autosave triggers are switched on, because playtime and scene memory are handled here too. It is marked so that it survives a scene change and does not appear in the Hierarchy. A game never needs to add it to a scene. Starting Shipready again hands the same runner the new settings.

SaveMigrationAttribute #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveMigrationAttribute : Attribute

Marks a static method as the step that upgrades a save from one version to the next.

The method takes a SaveTree and nothing else. That is deliberate: a migration edits the saved data rather than the game classes, so a step written today still works after those classes have been renamed, split or deleted.

Migrations run on a background thread, together with the rest of the file work, so a step must only edit the tree and must not touch Unity objects.

[SaveMigration(fromVersion: 3)]
static void RenameCash(SaveTree save) => save.RenameKeyEverywhere("cash", "money");

Constructors

SaveMigrationAttribute(int)
public SaveMigrationAttribute(int fromVersion);

Marks the method as the step from one save version to the next.

Parameter Description
fromVersion The version this step upgrades from. A step marked 3 turns a version 3 save into a version 4 save.

Properties

public string Description { get; set; }

A name for the step, used in reports and in the Console. Defaults to the method name.

The version this step upgrades from.

SavePoint #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SavePoint : MonoBehaviour

A checkpoint: saves when the player walks into its trigger, or when a UnityEvent calls SaveNow(), with a cooldown so walking back and forth does not save every step, and an "only once" option. Put it on an object with a trigger collider (3D or 2D) and tag the player Player; no code.

It writes the next autosave by default, or a chosen slot or the quicksave. The location name, when set, is what the slot card shows ("Old Mill"). The save runs in the background. Whether it has fired is not saved: give the object a Saveable with its Enabled saver, or switch it off from On Saved, to keep an only-once point used after a load.

Add Component menu: Shipready → Save Point

ReadObjectLink<T>(string, Action<T>)
public void ReadObjectLink<T>(string name, Action<T> assign) where T : UnityEngine.Object;

Reads back a link written with SaveWriter.WriteObjectLink(string, UnityEngine.Object), or by the Field Picker, and hands the object to assign.

Inside ISaveable.RestoreState(SaveReader), the link is settled in the second pass of the restore, once every saved object exists, including runtime objects the same load re-creates later; assign is called then, still before any Start runs. While a load is still loading its saved scenes, a link into a scene that has not loaded yet waits until every saved scene is in. Anywhere else, such as a reader from SaveKit.Data, the link is settled at once among the live objects (SaveWorld.Find(string)) and assign is called before this returns.

A link to an object that no longer exists, or that has no T, gives null and an SaveErrorCode.ObjectNotFound warning naming the value; an asset no longer registered gives null and SaveErrorCode.AssetNotRegistered. When the save does not hold name at all, assign is not called, so the field keeps its default. An exception thrown by assign becomes a warning.

Type parameter Description
T What the link is wanted as: GameObject, a component type, or an asset type.
Parameter Description
name The value name.
assign What to do with the object, usually setting a field. Null does nothing.

Example

public void RestoreState(SaveReader r)
{
    r.ReadObjectLink<Door>("door", d => door = d);
}

ReadObjectLinks<T>(string, Action<List<T>>)
public void ReadObjectLinks<T>(string name, Action<List<T>> assign) where T : UnityEngine.Object;

Reads back a list of links written with SaveWriter.WriteObjectLinks<T>(string, IList<T>) or by the Field Picker, and hands the list to assign, at the same moment and under the same rules as ReadObjectLink<T>(string, Action<T>). An entry whose object is gone is null in the list, with a warning, so the list keeps its length.

Type parameter Description
T What the entries are wanted as: GameObject, a component type, or an asset type.
Parameter Description
name The value name.
assign What to do with the new list. Null does nothing.

SaveWorld #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveWorld

The saved world: scene memory, the scene loader, and the hooks a pool or a custom scene loader needs. Reach it through SaveKit.World.

Scene memory keeps the state of scenes the player has left. A scene that loads during play gets its remembered state back automatically, before any Start runs. Leaving a scene through SaveKit.LoadScene(string, LoadSceneMode) or SaveKit.UnloadScene(Scene) captures it on the way out; a game with its own scene loading calls CaptureScene(Scene) first.

Example

SaveKit.World.CaptureScene(scene);           // before unloading a scene yourself
SceneManager.UnloadSceneAsync(scene);

pool.Release(enemy);
SaveKit.World.Despawned(enemy);               // a pooled object is not saved while it waits

How many seconds a load waits for one saved scene to load before it gives up on it, warns, and finishes with the scenes it has. Zero or less uses DefaultSceneLoadTimeoutSeconds. A scene that loads later still gets its saved state.

SlotIndex #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SlotIndex

A small cache of what each slot holds, so a menu with ninety-nine slots does not have to open ninety-nine files to draw itself.

It is only ever a cache. Each entry records the size and the time of the file it describes, and an entry is used only while both still match, so a save written by anything other than Shipready, a file restored from a cloud backup or a hand edit all make Shipready read the real file again. A cache that can go stale without noticing would show a player the wrong save, which is worse than being slow.

LoadSavedScenes 0 SaveKit.LoadAsync loads the scenes the save was made in, makes the saved active scene active, and restores each scene as it loads. The default.

Namespace RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Codecs #

AesHmacCodec #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Codecs · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class AesHmacCodec

Optional encryption for the data section of a save: AES-256 in CBC mode with a fresh random starting block for every write, and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the header and the encrypted bytes. Encrypt first, then sign, which is the order that makes the signature trustworthy.

The payload is laid out as the 16-byte starting block, then the encrypted bytes, then the 32-byte signature. A single changed byte anywhere in it fails the signature check.

Encryption here stops a player opening a save in a text editor and changing their gold. It is not anti-cheat and must never be used for passwords or payment details: the passphrase ships inside the game, and a Mono build is straightforward to decompile.

How many bytes the random starting block takes at the front of the payload.

How many bytes of the key check value are stored in a save header.

MacBytes
public const int MacBytes = 32;

How many bytes the signature takes at the end of the payload.

GzipCodec #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Codecs · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class GzipCodec

GZip compression for the data section of a save. Compression is off by default because a typical save is already small, but JSON compresses several times over, so a large world is worth packing.

The output is deterministic: the same input always produces the same bytes, which keeps the acceptance tests able to compare files directly.

KeyDerivation #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Codecs · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class KeyDerivation

Turns a developer passphrase into encryption keys, once per run.

Stretching the passphrase with PBKDF2 takes a noticeable fraction of a second on purpose, so the result is cached: the first encrypted save pays for it and the rest do not. The cache is cleared when static state resets, so turning off domain reload cannot leave a stale key behind after the passphrase is changed in the Inspector.

This is not anti-cheat. The passphrase ships inside the game, so a determined player can find it, especially in a Mono build. What it does do is stop a save being edited in a text editor, and notice when one has been.

ISaveAuthority #

interface in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Coop · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public interface ISaveAuthority

Decides who may save and load world data. In co-op only the host may; a solo game needs no authority at all, because SaveKit.Authority left at null always allows it.

When the authority says no, every slot, autosave and quicksave save, load and delete returns SaveErrorCode.HostOnly without touching storage. Saving and loading the global file stays allowed, so a client keeps its own settings.

Example

sealed class NgoAuthority : ISaveAuthority
{
    public bool HasSaveAuthority { get { return NetworkManager.Singleton.IsServer; } }
}
SaveKit.Authority = new NgoAuthority();

ISpawnHandler #

interface in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Coop · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public interface ISpawnHandler

Creates and removes runtime objects for Shipready. A load re-creates the objects that were spawned at runtime through this hook, so a pool, a network library or Addressables can make them. Left at null, Shipready uses Instantiate and Destroy.

Shipready gives the new object its saved id itself, straight after Spawn(GameObject, Vector3, Quaternion, Transform) returns, so the hook only has to make the object.

PlayerData #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Coop · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class PlayerData

Per-player data in a co-op game: position, inventory, anything that belongs to one player rather than to the world. The host keeps it, under the stable id the game supplies (see IPlayerIdentity), and it is saved inside the host's slot beside the categories, as players.<player id>.<category>.

A save writes each player's values for every category it saves; a load brings them back, so a player who rejoins gets their data again and a player the save does not know starts from defaults. Reach it through SaveKit.Players.

Example

SaveData mine = SaveKit.Players.For(steamId);
mine.Set("position", transform.position, "Progress");
Vector3 back = SaveKit.Players.For(steamId).Get("position", spawnPoint, "Progress");

SaveNode #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Data · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveNode

One node of the save tree, which is Shipready data model that everything else reads: the JSON writer and reader, the menu, the Save Inspector, Diagnostics and migrations.

Numbers are held as the exact text they were written with rather than as a Double. That is what makes a Single come back bit-exact, keeps a Int64 past 2^53 intact, and makes a readable save look the way a developer expects instead of showing 0.100000001490116 where the game wrote 0.1.

Object members keep their insertion order, so writing the same tree twice always produces the same bytes. The checksum relies on that.

MeasureDepth(int)
public int MeasureDepth(int limit);

How deeply this subtree nests, counting this node as level 1, stopping as soon as the limit is passed.

Shipready reads files only up to a fixed nesting limit, so it has to refuse to write a tree deeper than that. Writing one would produce a file that verifies as correct and then can never be read back, which is a far worse failure than refusing the save.

Parameter Description
limit The depth to stop counting at. The result is never more than this plus one, which is enough to tell that the limit was passed.

Returns: The nesting depth, capped just above the limit.

ValueConverters #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Data · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class ValueConverters

Turns the supported value types into save tree nodes and back. Every number, date and identifier goes through here, which is how Shipready keeps one promise that quietly breaks a lot of save systems: the file is byte-identical whatever language the machine is set to.

A float is written with the fewest significant digits, seven, eight or nine, that read back as exactly the same float, and a double with fifteen, sixteen or seventeen; so a readable save shows 0.8 where the game stored 0.8f, and still reads back bit-exact. Whole numbers are written as whole numbers, and negative zero as -0. Decimals keep every digit. NaN and infinity have no JSON spelling, so they are written as the strings NaN, Infinity and -Infinity.

The one culture every number, date and identifier in a save is written with.

DateTimeFormat
public const string DateTimeFormat = "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffffffZ";

The format a DateTime is written with: round-trip, always UTC.

DoubleFormat
public const string DoubleFormat = "G17";

The longest format a Double is written with: seventeen significant digits always read back bit-exact. Shorter text is written whenever it reads back the same.

HeaderDateTimeFormat
public const string HeaderDateTimeFormat = "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ";

The shorter date format used for the savedUtc field of a save header.

SingleFormat
public const string SingleFormat = "G9";

The longest format a Single is written with: nine significant digits always read back bit-exact. Shorter text is written whenever it reads back the same.

TimeSpanFormat

The format a TimeSpan is written with: round-trip and readable.

PlayModeToast #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Diagnostics · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class PlayModeToast : MonoBehaviour

The Editor's Play Mode toast: a short note at the top of the Game view after each save or load, such as "Saved Slot 1: 12 objects, 3 values". Clicking it raises Clicked, which Shipready's editor tools answer by opening the Save Inspector on that report. Shipready's editor code adds it at the start of Play Mode when the toasts are switched on (Tools → Shipready → Saves → Play Mode Toasts). Editor only: this class does not exist in builds, so nothing of it can reach a player.

SaveLog #

public static class SaveLog

The one place Shipready writes to the Console. Every line carries the product prefix and, where there is one, the SK identifier, so a developer can search for it.

Properties

How much is written to the Console. Defaults to SaveLogLevel.Warnings.

RecentReports
public static IReadOnlyList<SaveReport> RecentReports { get; }

The reports of the most recent saves and loads of this play session, oldest first, at most RecentReportCapacity. Every finished save and load is kept whatever the log level, so the Save Inspector can list them even while the Console stays quiet. The list is a snapshot that never changes after it is handed out.

ReportToConsole
public static bool ReportToConsole { get; set; }

Whether every save and load prints a one-line report (SaveReport.ToSummaryLine(SaveErrorCode, bool)) to the Console at SaveLogLevel.Warnings and above. Off by default, so the Console stays quiet; Shipready copies SaveKitSettings.ReportToConsole here when it starts. At SaveLogLevel.Verbose the line is always printed, with the time of each stage added. At SaveLogLevel.Errors and SaveLogLevel.Off nothing is printed.

SaveProfilerMarkers #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Diagnostics · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class SaveProfilerMarkers

The names of the Profiler markers Shipready wraps around each stage of a save and a load, so every stage shows up in Unity's Profiler, on the thread it ran on. Capture and Restore run on the main thread; the others run on the background thread a save or load uses.

A save: Capture (gathering the values), Serialize (the tree to JSON), Compress, Encrypt, Write (every disk write, swap, backup move and delete) and Verify (reading the temporary file back and checking it, after the temporary file is written and before it is swapped into place). Verify sits beside the Write samples, not inside them, and its own disk read shows as a Read inside it. A load: Read (every disk read), Decrypt, Decompress, Parse (JSON to the tree and the checksum check), Migrate and Restore (putting the values back into the game).

The markers cost next to nothing while the Profiler is not recording. A game can read them with ProfilerRecorder or Recorder.Get by these names.

Reading the temporary file back and checking it before it is swapped into place.

Write

Writing to the disk: the temporary file, the swap, the backups, thumbnails and the slot cache.

AtomicFileWriter #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Files · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class AtomicFileWriter

Writes a save file so that a crash can never leave a player without one.

The promise is that at every moment during a save, at least one complete, valid copy exists on disk. The new bytes go to a temporary file first and are read back and checked against what Shipready meant to write. Only then is the temporary file swapped into place in a single step, with the file it replaces parked under a staging name. The backups are shuffled down afterwards, never before, so a save that fails at the swap has destroyed nothing. Cut the power at any point and the next load finds either the new save or the previous one, never half of either.

Methods

public static AtomicWriteOutcome Write(ISaveStorage storage, string mainName, byte[] bytes, int backupCount);

Parameter Description

mainName The main file name, for example slot_01.save.
bytes The finished file contents.
backupCount How many rotating backups to keep, from 0 to 5.

Returns: What happened, including which step it reached.

AtomicWriteStep #

enum in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Files · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public enum AtomicWriteStep

The steps of a crash-safe write, in the order they run.

Values

Name Value Description
NotStarted 0 Nothing has happened yet.
WriteTemporary 1 Writing the temporary file.
VerifyTemporary 2 Reading the temporary file back and checking it.
Swap 3 Swapping the temporary file into place and parking the file it replaced. Everything a player could lose is still intact up to the moment this step succeeds.
RotateBackups 4 Moving the existing backups down a number. The new save is already in place.
StoreBackup 5 Turning the parked file into the newest backup.
PruneBackups 6 Removing backups past the configured count.
Done 7 The save is in place.

BackupRotator #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Files · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class BackupRotator

Keeps the rotating backups for one save file. Two are kept by default, which is one more copy than almost any player needs and still costs nothing worth measuring.

Rotation happens just before a new save is swapped into place: the oldest backup is dropped, the rest shuffle down a number, and the file being replaced becomes the newest backup. At no point is more than one copy in motion, so a crash during rotation still leaves a complete save on disk.

RecoveryLoader #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Files · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class RecoveryLoader

Reads a save, falling back through every copy Shipready keeps until one works.

The order is the main file, then a complete temporary file left behind by a save that was cut short, then each backup from newest to oldest. The first valid copy wins, and the result says which one it was, so the menu can show "Restored from backup" and the game can tell the player what happened.

A damaged main file is moved aside rather than deleted, because a player who has lost progress deserves to have somebody able to look at the file. When every copy is damaged, nothing at all is touched.

Methods

public static RecoveryOutcome Load(ISaveStorage storage, string mainName, SaveFileOptions options, bool acceptEditedFiles, bool quarantineDamagedMain);

Reads a save, trying each copy in turn.

When SaveFileOptions.AutomaticFallback is off, only the main file is read: a damaged or missing main file fails with the damage code and nothing is moved aside, so the player can choose to restore a backup instead.

Parameter Description
storage Where the files live.
mainName The main file name.
options The file options to read with. Null uses the defaults.
acceptEditedFiles Whether a file whose checksum no longer matches should be loaded anyway. The Editor passes true so a developer can edit a save while testing.
quarantineDamagedMain Whether to move a damaged main file aside once a backup has loaded successfully.

Returns: What happened, including the save on success.

SaveEnvelope #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Files · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class SaveEnvelope

The file format. A readable save is plain JSON that any text editor opens. A compressed or encrypted save is a short binary marker, then a readable header, then the packed data, so the menu can still read slot info without unpacking anything.

The loader tells the two apart from the first bytes, which is what lets a game turn compression or encryption on in an update without stranding the saves players already have.

SaveFileStore #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Files · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveFileStore

One save file, read and written safely. This is the layer the slots, the menu and the Save Inspector all sit on: it packs and unpacks the envelope, keeps the backups, falls back when a file is damaged, and makes sure two saves of the same file never overlap.

Work that does not need Unity runs on a background thread. Requests for the same file are queued and run in the order they arrived, so a quicksave fired twice in a second leaves the second one on disk, not the first.

options The file options to use. Null uses the defaults.

Puts the newest valid backup of a damaged save back in place as the main file, and waits for it to finish.

The backup's bytes are copied unchanged through the crash-safe write (temporary file, read back and check, one swap), so the restored file keeps the backup's save time. The damaged main file is kept aside as .corrupt-<time>, and the backups stay where they are. A main file that reads correctly is never replaced.

The bookkeeping at the front of every save file: which envelope format it uses, which save version the game was on, when it was written, how it is packed, and the checksum that proves it is intact.

SaveMergeJob #

abstract class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Files · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public abstract class SaveMergeJob

Builds the save to write from the copy already on disk, for SaveFileStore.WriteMerged(string, SaveMergeJob) and SaveFileStore.WriteMergedAsync(string, SaveMergeJob).

Both methods run on a background thread, inside the queue for the file, so nothing else can read or write the file between reading what is there and writing what replaces it. Neither may touch Unity objects. Everything a job needs from the game has to be gathered on the main thread before the job is handed over.

Reads JSON back into a save tree. It never throws: a file that is not JSON comes back as a failure with the position and reason, which the recovery loader turns into a damaged file result and moves on to the next copy.

JsonTextWriter #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Json · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class JsonTextWriter

Writes a save tree as JSON. Shipready has its own writer rather than using JsonUtility for the whole file, because the tree has to come back exactly as it went in: member order preserved, numbers in the text they were written with, and nothing that depends on the machine language settings.

Compact output is deterministic: the same tree always produces the same bytes. The checksum in the save header is measured over compact output, so turning pretty-printing on or off never changes a checksum.

MigrationRunner #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Migration · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class MigrationRunner

Runs the migration steps that bring an old save up to the version the game is on.

Steps run in order, one version at a time, so a save from three versions ago passes through every step in between rather than needing its own special case. A gap in that chain is reported rather than guessed at: loading a save the game only half understands is how progress gets quietly mangled.

A step can arrive two ways: added by hand with Add(int, Action<SaveTree>, string), or found through the [SaveMigration] attribute. A step added by hand always wins over a found one for the same version, whichever was registered first. Two found steps for the same version are a mistake in the game, so only the first one in a fixed order (assembly name, then type name, then method name) is used and the Console names both.

Properties

How many versions have a step, counting each version once.

Parameter Description

step What to do to the save.

Adds a step by hand, or replaces the step already added by hand for that version. A step added by hand always wins over one found through [SaveMigration], whether it is added before or after Shipready starts, so a game can override a step Shipready discovered automatically.

Parameter Description
fromVersion The version this step upgrades from. Must be 1 or more.
step What to do to the save. Null is ignored. It runs on a background thread, so it must only edit the tree and must not touch Unity objects.

DiscoverInLoadedAssemblies()
public int DiscoverInLoadedAssemblies();

Looks through every loaded assembly for static methods marked [SaveMigration] and registers them.

The assemblies, types and methods are walked in a fixed order (assembly name, then type name, then method name), so the same project always registers the same steps. When two methods are marked for the same version, only the first is registered and a warning names both. Running this again finds the same methods and adds nothing.

A build with code stripping switched on can remove a method nothing appears to call, which is why Shipready also writes a link file during a build listing the types these methods live in.

Returns: How many steps were added.

DiscoverInType(Type)
public int DiscoverInType(Type type);

Looks through one type for static methods marked [SaveMigration]. Steps found this way follow the same rules as automatic discovery: a step added by hand still wins, and a second method for a version that already has a found step is ignored with a warning.

Parameter Description
type The type to look in. Null does nothing.

Returns: How many steps were added.

SaveFileOptions #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Settings · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveFileOptions

How save files are written: readable or packed, how many backups to keep, the extension, and what to do about a file that has been edited.

The settings asset holds two sets: SaveKitSettings.FileOptions for the slots, the autosaves and the quicksave, and SaveKitSettings.GlobalFileOptions, which the global settings file uses instead when SaveKitSettings.UseSlotOptionsForGlobalFile is off. A SaveFileStore applies one set to every file unless it is given a set for a particular file.

Changing any of these in a game update never strands existing saves. Each file records how it was packed (readable, compressed, encrypted), and the loader follows the file rather than the settings. Only the passphrase has to stay the same for encrypted files.

Properties

AutomaticFallback
public bool AutomaticFallback { get; set; }

Whether a load falls back to the newest valid backup on its own when the main file is damaged. On by default: the player gets the backup, the damaged file is kept aside as .corrupt-<time>, and the result says SaveErrorCode.RecoveredFromBackup.

When off, a damaged or missing main file of a slot, an autosave or the quicksave is never replaced by a backup on load. The load fails with the damage code, nothing is moved aside, and the slot info reports SlotInfo.IsDamaged and SlotInfo.HasValidBackup, so the menu can offer Restore backup, which calls SaveKit.RestoreBackup(int).

The global file, which holds the player's settings, always falls back, whatever this says. Saving over a damaged slot also works the same either way: the save keeps the categories it does not write from the newest valid copy, and the damaged file is kept aside.

With fallback off, a crash during the very first save of a slot, before the new file was swapped into place, leaves only the temporary file (.tmp). The slot then lists as damaged and its load reports damage (SK101); Restore backup puts that temporary file in place, because it counts as a backup.

BackupCount
public int BackupCount { get; set; }

How many rotating backups to keep per file, from 0 to 5. Two by default, which is one more copy than most players ever need and still almost no disk space.

ChecksumPolicy
public ChecksumPolicy ChecksumPolicy { get; set; }

What to do about a readable save that no longer matches its own checksum.

Compress
public bool Compress { get; set; }

Whether the data section is GZip compressed. Off by default, because a typical save is small; worth turning on for a large world.

Encrypt
public bool Encrypt { get; set; }

Whether the data section is encrypted with a tamper check. Off by default. This stops a player editing a save in a text editor; it is not anti-cheat, because the key ships inside the game.

EncryptSlotInfo
public bool EncryptSlotInfo { get; set; }

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Settings · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class SaveKitSettings : ScriptableObject

Every choice a game makes about saving, in one asset. The Setup Wizard creates it and fills it in; Shipready reads it and never writes to it at runtime.

The asset lives in a Resources folder in the game own project, not inside the Shipready folder, so that updating Shipready never overwrites a developer settings.

Whether every slot save, autosave and quicksave gets a thumbnail. On by default. Before a slot save, autosave or quicksave that has no picture set with SaveKit.SetNextThumbnail(Texture2D), Shipready renders SaveKit.ThumbnailCamera, or Camera.main when none is set, into a 320×180 picture on the main thread. Without a camera or a graphics device (a server or a -nographics run) there is simply no picture, and on a phone or handheld being suspended no picture is taken, because the game may no longer draw then. Switch it off to keep saves free of that rendering or to set the pictures yourself.

How save files are written: readable or packed, how many backups, and the extension. These are the options of the slots, the autosaves and the quicksave, and of the global settings file too unless UseSlotOptionsForGlobalFile is off.

GlobalFileExtension

The extension of the global settings file: the slots' one, unless the global file has its own options and extension.

public string GlobalFileName { get; }

The file name for the global file, including the extension: the slots' extension, or the global file's own one (see GlobalFileExtension).

GlobalFileOptions
public SaveFileOptions GlobalFileOptions { get; set; }

The global settings file's own options, used when UseSlotOptionsForGlobalFile is off: pretty-printing, compression, encryption (and of the slot info), backups, checksum policy and file extension. An empty extension means the slots' extension.

The passphrase, salt and key iterations here are never used: every file of a game shares the key from FileOptions, so a settings file written under either setting can always be read. Switching between the two never strands an old file either, because each file records how it was packed; and when the extension changes, Shipready loads whichever of the old and the new settings file was written last, so the player's latest settings come back, and the next save writes the new name. The old file is left where it is. Shipready reads these options when it starts.

Whether Shipready starts by itself when the game runs, just before the first scene loads, using this asset from its Resources folder. On by default, so a game made with the Setup Wizard saves without any code. Switch it off to start Shipready yourself with SaveKit.Initialise(), for example after choosing a profile folder. Calling SaveKit.Initialise() while it is on is fine: Shipready simply starts again with the settings given.

A folder inside the save folder that keeps one player's saves apart from another's on a shared machine. Empty, the default, means everybody on the machine shares one save folder.

{profile} in it is replaced, when Shipready starts, by SaveKit.ProfileId, which the game sets at runtime, for example to the player's Steam ID. So {profile} saves Steam user 76561198000000000 into Saves/76561198000000000, the folder a Steam Auto-Cloud subdirectory of Saves/{64BitSteamID} matches. Steam itself fills in nothing here: Shipready only knows the id the game gives it. Text without {profile} is used as it is, as one fixed folder name. See ResolveProfileFolder(string, string, string).

Off by default, so the Console stays quiet; every report is still in the Save Inspector's Recent saves and loads. It prints at SaveLogLevel.Warnings and SaveLogLevel.Verbose (Verbose adds the time of each stage); at Errors and Off nothing is printed. The warnings themselves are always printed as warnings at Warnings and above, whatever this says. Copied into SaveLog.ReportToConsole when Shipready starts.

FileSaveStorage #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Storage · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class FileSaveStorage : ISaveStorage

Save files on the local disk, under a folder inside Application.persistentDataPath. This is what a shipped game uses.

Writes are flushed all the way to the disk rather than left in the operating system cache, because the next step in a save verifies what was written and the step after that swaps it into place. A write that is still in a cache would make both of those lies.

ISaveStorage #

interface in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Storage · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public interface ISaveStorage

Where save files live. Shipready ships a file storage for the real game and a memory storage for tests; a platform that needs something else, such as browser storage or a cloud service, can plug in here without the rest of Shipready changing.

Names handed to these calls are plain file names inside the storage, never full paths, so the same save code works whatever the storage is.

Nothing here throws. Every call reports what happened, because a save system that throws when a disk fills up is a save system that loses saves.

MemorySaveStorage #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Storage · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public sealed class MemorySaveStorage : ISaveStorage

Save files held in memory. Shipready tests run against this, and a game can use it to test its own save and load code without writing anything to disk.

It can also be told to fail. That is what the reliability tests use to reproduce a full disk, a denied folder and a crash part way through a save: set FailAfterOperations to the step to fail at, and every file is left exactly as it was at that moment.

How many operations to let through before failing, or -1 to never fail. Counting starts at zero, so a value of 0 fails the very first operation.

FieldSaver #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.World · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public static class FieldSaver

The Field Picker saver: saves the Inspector fields ticked on a Saveable. It only accepts fields Unity itself saves (public or [SerializeField], not [NonSerialized], not static, not read-only) of a type Shipready supports:

  • numbers, text, true/false, enums and the Unity vector, rotation, colour, rectangle and bounds types;
  • classes and structs marked [Serializable], saved under Unity's own rules;
  • links to saved objects (a Saveable, its GameObject or one of its components) and to registered assets such as ScriptableObjects and prefabs;
  • lists and arrays of any of those.

The Field Picker greys out every other field and shows the reason this class gives.

ISceneLoader #

interface in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.World · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save

public interface ISceneLoader

Loads scenes for Shipready, for a game that starts its scene loads its own way, such as scenes that are not in Build Settings or a load that also shows a loading screen. Set it on SaveWorld.SceneLoader. Left at null, Shipready loads scenes that are in Build Settings with SceneManager.LoadSceneAsync.

Return the AsyncOperation of a SceneManager load, and leave allowSceneActivation on: Shipready waits for the operation to finish, up to SaveWorld.SceneLoadTimeoutSeconds. A game that loads scenes through Addressables loads them itself and uses WorldLoadMode.RestoreIntoCurrentScenes, or calls SaveWorld.ApplyScene(Scene) once each scene is in.

The yes-or-no question the menu asks before anything that cannot be undone: overwriting a save, loading over unsaved progress, deleting. GameMenu #

public sealed class GameMenu : MonoBehaviour

A title screen or pause menu that needs no code: Continue (the newest save of any kind, greyed out when there is none), New Game, Save Game and Load Game (they open your SaveMenu), Delete All Saves and Quit. MenuText #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public sealed class MenuText : ScriptableObject

Every word the save menu shows, in one asset, so translating the menu needs no extra package: duplicate DefaultMenuText, translate the copy and assign it to the menu (SaveMenu.Text), or swap assets when the player changes language.

Lines with {0} are formatted with string.Format: {0} is the slot's name in the questions, the date in RestoredFromBackupStatus, and so on, as each field says. Dates use DateFormat in the culture DateCultureName names (invariant by default).

Create menu: Assets → Create → Shipready → Menu Text

MenuTheme #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public sealed class MenuTheme : ScriptableObject

How the save menu looks: every colour, the font, the font sizes, the corner radius and the spacing, in one asset. Change a value here and every panel, card, button and badge follows, because each of them carries a ThemedElement that reads it.

The easy way to restyle is Tools > Shipready > Menu Style: pick one of six ready-made styles, change any colour, size or the layout (Layout), and see it at once. It works on a copy in your data folder, never on Shipready's own assets. By hand: duplicate DefaultMenuTheme, change the copy and assign it to the menu (SaveMenu.Theme). For changes the theme cannot express, edit a prefab variant of SaveMenu.prefab, or build your own menu on the public API.

Create menu: Assets → Create → Shipready → Menu Theme

MessageIcons #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public static class MessageIcons

Shipready's built-in icons, one for each MessageKind: a spinner for saving and loading, a tick for saved, a document with a crack for damaged, a padlock, two people for co-op, and so on. They are drawn from exact shapes when first asked for, so Shipready ships no image files: every line has the same weight and smooth edges, the shape sits exactly in the middle of its square, and the big texture with its smaller copies stays crisp from a small badge up to a 4K screen.

Each icon is white on a clear background, so an Image's colour tints it. A theme can replace any of them (MessageKindLook.Icon). The cache is cleared when a play session starts, so it is correct with domain reload switched off.

The kinds of message Shipready shows the player. Each has its own colour and icon in the theme (MenuTheme.ContextColour(MessageKind), MenuTheme.IconFor(MessageKind)) and its own short words in the menu text (MenuText.ShortWords(MessageKind)).

Values

Name Value Description
Saving 0 A save is running.
Saved 1 A save worked.
SaveFailed 2 A save did not work.
Loading 3 A load is running.
Loaded 4 A load worked.
LoadFailed 5 A load did not work.
Restored 6 A save came back from its backup.
Damaged 7 A save cannot be read.
Autosave 8 An autosave.
Quicksave 9 The quicksave.
NewerVersion 10 A save made by a newer version of the game.
CoOp 11 Co-op: only the host can save or load.
Locked 12 Saving or loading is not possible right now.
Info 13 Any other news, such as "Deleted Slot 2."

public sealed class MessageLook

How Shipready's messages look, on the MenuTheme (MenuTheme.Messages): how each part shows its messages (DisplayAs), where the saving indicator and the save notes sit, the colour of each state and each kind's icon. Set it once in the theme; the indicator, the notes and the menu can each choose their own on top.

The colours of the Autosave, Damaged, Restored and From a newer version states are the theme's badge colours, so a badge and its icon always match.

MessageView #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public sealed class MessageView : MonoBehaviour, ILayoutElement

Shows one message the way the theme asks (DisplayAs): its full or short words, its icon (plain or in the state's colour), both, or nothing. The saving indicator, the save notes, the menu's status line and the slot card badges are each one of these.

It lays its icon and words out itself, so they are always exactly centred: the block is in the middle of the box, the icon's middle sits level with the middle of the capital letters, and a turning icon turns about its own centre. Laying out happens only when the message changes, never each frame.

Add Component menu: Shipready → Message View

OrientationScaler #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public sealed class OrientationScaler : MonoBehaviour

Sits beside a kit canvas's Canvas Scaler and picks its reference size for the screen: the 1920×1080 design on a wide screen, and on a screen held upright (with the layout's MenuLayout.Portrait on Auto or Custom) a narrow one, so a phone gets words and buttons it can read and press. The menus listen to Changed and lay themselves out again. It checks the canvas's size every frame and acts only when it changes, as when a phone turns; it allocates nothing.

PortraitLayout #

enum in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public enum PortraitLayout

How Shipready's menus lay out on a screen held upright (taller than wide), such as a phone.

Values

Name Value Description
Auto 0 A phone layout: the menus are drawn for a 760-unit-wide screen, so words and buttons are as big as a phone needs (body text about 31 pixels and buttons about 90 on a 1080-wide phone), the save menu fills the width with one column of tiles, and the Game Menu takes most of it. The default.
Landscape 1 The same layout as a wide screen, scaled down to fit the width.
Custom 2 The phone layout, drawn for the width of your choice (MenuLayout.PortraitWidth).

RoundedSprites #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public static class RoundedSprites

Makes the rounded shapes the menu is drawn with, so Shipready ships no sprite assets: a filled rounded rectangle and a rounded outline for any radius, as small 9-sliced sprites with anti-aliased corners. Each shape is made once and cached for the rest of the run.

The cache is cleared when a play session starts, so it is correct with domain reload switched off.

SafeAreaPanel #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public sealed class SafeAreaPanel : MonoBehaviour

Keeps a panel inside the screen's safe area: clear of a phone's notch, rounded corners and the home bar, and of a TV's overscan. It shrinks its own rectangle to Screen.safeArea, so everything under it (the save menu, the Game Menu, the saving indicator, the save notes) stays where the player can see and reach it. On a screen with no unsafe edges it fills the whole screen, so nothing changes. It checks again when the screen or its safe area changes, and allocates nothing.

Only a screen-space canvas is fitted; a world-space one (such as a preview in the Editor) is left whole. Simulated tries an inset without a phone.

Add Component menu: Shipready → Safe Area Panel

Properties

Area
public Rect Area { get; }

The part of its canvas this panel covers now, from (0, 0) to (1, 1).

Simulated
public static Rect? Simulated { get; set; }

A safe area to use instead of the screen's, as a share of the screen from (0, 0) bottom left to (1, 1) top right, such as new Rect(0.04f, 0.05f, 0.92f, 0.9f); null uses the screen's own. For trying a phone's insets on a desktop, and for tests. Applies to every Safe Area at once.

SaveMenu #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public sealed class SaveMenu : MonoBehaviour

The player's save and load menu: one prefab, two modes. Drop SaveMenu.prefab into a scene and call Open(SaveMenuMode) from a pause menu or a main menu.

  • Save mode lists the manual slots. An empty slot saves at once; a used one asks "Overwrite?" first. A thumbnail is taken just before the menu shows.
  • Load mode lists the autosaves (newest first), the quicksave, then the manual slots that hold a save, then the empty ones, dimmed. Loading asks first whether unsaved progress may be lost (ConfirmLoad).
  • Every card with a save can be deleted, after a confirmation. A damaged save loads through its backup and the status line says "Restored from backup (date)"; with automatic fallback switched off it offers Restore backup instead. A save from a newer version of the game shows a badge and cannot be loaded.
  • A co-op client (SaveKit.CanSave false) sees the cards without their buttons and a line saying only the host can save.

Mouse, touch, keyboard and gamepad all work, with the old Input Manager or the Input System: every button is a uGUI selectable on explicit navigation, so whichever input module the EventSystem has drives it. When the scene has no EventSystem the menu makes one. Cancel closes the open confirmation, or else the menu. Restyle it with a MenuTheme, translate it with a MenuText.

The menu holds no static state, so several can exist and it is safe with domain reload switched off. In Load Saved Scenes mode a load replaces the scenes, so keep the menu in a scene that stays loaded, or under DontDestroyOnLoad, if it should report the result.

Add Component menu: Shipready → Save Menu

Close()

Makes sure the scene has an EventSystem, which uGUI needs for any input at all. When there is none, one is made with an InputSystemUIInputModule when the Input System is the active input handler, otherwise a StandaloneInputModule. The menu calls this when it opens.

Backs out one step, as Cancel (Escape, or East on a gamepad) does: closes the open confirmation, or else the menu. At most once per frame, so one key press never closes both. While a save or load started from the menu is running, the menu closes once it has finished. ConsumedCancelThisFrame is true afterwards for the rest of the frame.

SaveNotes #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.UI

public sealed class SaveNotes : MonoBehaviour

A short note to the player when a load finished ("Game loaded"), when a save came back from its backup, or when a save or a load did not work, shown for a moment at the edge of the screen. The saving indicator already shows saves, so saves that worked are off by default. Drop SaveNotes.prefab into your first scene; it stays across scene loads. No code.

Like the indicator, it takes its colours, icons and font from the MenuTheme and its words from the MenuText. The theme says how it shows (DisplayAs) and where it sits (top centre by default); tick Own Display or Own Position to choose for these notes alone. Switch the component off to hide them.

Namespace RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Build #

MigrationLinkXmlBuilder #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Build · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Core

public sealed class MigrationLinkXmlBuilder : IUnityLinkerProcessor

Keeps migration steps alive through code stripping.

Nothing in a game calls a migration directly: Shipready finds them by looking for the [SaveMigration] attribute. Code stripping cannot see that, so in an IL2CPP build with stripping turned up it would remove the very methods that let an old save load. This adds a link file during the build naming every type that holds one, which is the supported way to tell the stripper to leave something alone.

The file is written to the project's Temp/RareGeometry.Shipready.Save folder, which Unity clears when the Editor closes, and handed to the linker by path, so nothing is left behind in the project. If it cannot be written the build log says so as an error, because a build without it can silently lose the migrations.

Properties

Where this step runs relative to other build callbacks.

Constants

LinkFileName

The name of the generated link file.

Methods

FindMigrationTypes()
public static Dictionary<string, List<string>> FindMigrationTypes();

Every type holding a method marked [SaveMigration], grouped by the assembly it lives in. Only assemblies that go into a player are included, which leaves out Editor and test assemblies whatever they are called. Type names are written the way the linker expects them, with / between a nested type and the type around it. Exposed so Diagnostics can report the same list.

Returns: Assembly name to type names, both in ordinal order. Never null.

Namespace RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Registries #

RegistryUpkeep #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Registries · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Core

public static class RegistryUpkeep

Keeps the Prefab, Asset and Scene Registries in step with the project, and keeps the Saveable ids on prefab assets right.

Prefabs. A Saveable on the root of a prefab asset carries the prefab's asset GUID as its prefab id, and the prefab is listed in the Prefab Registry under that GUID. A Saveable on a child carries a prefab-local id that is unique inside the prefab and never changes once given. No Saveable on a prefab asset carries an object id: those belong to scene objects only. Prefabs are checked whenever Unity imports them, and saved again only when something has to change. Prefabs whose asset is deleted leave the registry.

Scenes. Every scene in Build Settings is listed in the Scene Registry under its asset GUID, with its path as a label, and so is any scene registered by hand with RegisterScene(SceneAsset). When a listed scene is moved or renamed its path is updated, so the GUID that saves are keyed by still finds it. Deleted scenes leave the registry.

Assets. The Asset Registry is curated: assets are added with RegisterAsset(AssetRegistry, UnityEngine.Object) (Diagnostics offers it), and upkeep only removes entries whose asset is gone.

The registries are the ones the settings asset (Resources/ShipreadySaveSettings) points at. While it has none, the registries are left alone; prefab ids are still kept right. Automatic upkeep is not recorded for Undo: moving, renaming or deleting an asset cannot be undone either, and an Undo that put back an old scene path would quietly break old saves.
