SaveableDuplicateScan #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Registries · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Core

public static class SaveableDuplicateScan

Keeps every Saveable in the open scenes on its own id while you edit.

A Saveable fixes its own id when it wakes, but an inactive object never wakes, so a copy of an inactive object would keep the original's id. This scan runs after any change to the Hierarchy, at most once per Editor update and never in Play Mode. It looks at every Saveable in every loaded scene, inactive ones included, and gives a new id to any that has none or shares one with another.

Who keeps a shared id. The Saveable that held the id when the scan last ran keeps it, so the original keeps its id however the copy is moved around. When the scan has not seen the id before (a scene just opened, or the first scan after scripts reload), the first Saveable in scene order keeps it: scenes in the order the Hierarchy lists them, then objects from top to bottom, parents before their children. A copy made with Duplicate sits just below its original, so the original still wins.

Objects that Unity never saves (HideFlags.DontSaveInEditor) are left alone. A fix made by the automatic scan joins the undo step of the change that caused it, so one Undo removes both.

Properties

Enabled
public static bool Enabled { get; set; }

Whether the scan runs by itself after Hierarchy changes. On by default. A tool that needs duplicates to stay for a moment (a test of Diagnostics, for example) can switch it off and must switch it back on. ScanLoadedScenes() works either way.

Methods

ScanLoadedScenes()
public static int ScanLoadedScenes();

Scans every loaded scene now and gives a new id to each Saveable whose id is empty or already taken (see the class description for who keeps a shared id). Each fix is recorded for Undo and marks its scene as changed. Does nothing in Play Mode.

Returns: How many Saveables were given a new id.

SaveableEditorHooksInstaller #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Registries · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Core

public static class SaveableEditorHooksInstaller

Connects the Saveable component to the Editor.

The runtime code cannot use Editor API, yet a Saveable has to know two Editor-only things when it gives itself an id in Edit Mode: whether it is part of a prefab asset or a prefab being edited (those never carry an object id), and how to tell Unity that its scene changed so the new id is saved. This class answers both, and Unity installs it whenever scripts load.

Marking dirty is deferred to the next Editor update, because a Saveable gives itself an id from Reset, OnValidate or Awake, where Unity does not allow scene changes. Nothing is marked in Play Mode, and objects destroyed in the meantime are skipped.

Methods

public static void Install();

Points the Saveable's Editor hooks at this class. Unity does this when scripts load; calling it again does no harm.

Whether a Saveable belongs to a prefab rather than to a scene: it is part of a prefab asset, it is not in any valid scene, or it is in a preview scene such as Prefab Mode. Such a Saveable keeps its object id empty.

Parameter Description
saveable The Saveable to check.

Returns: true for a prefab asset or prefab-editing context. false for a scene object and for null. When Unity cannot answer, true: the duplicate scan gives a scene object its id later, while an id on a prefab asset would be wrong for good.

DiagnosticsRunner #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Diagnostics · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor

public static class DiagnosticsRunner

Runs every Diagnostics check over a DiagnosticsScope and hands back the issues found, each with a plain-English message and, where it is safe, a one-click fix that is recorded for Undo.

Scenes that are not open are read one at a time into a preview scene (on Unity 2022.3, opened beside the open scenes for a moment and closed again unsaved), with the Editor's automatic id repair paused, so two copies of an id are never loaded together and nothing quietly gives one of them a new id and hides the problem. The open scenes are the same afterwards. Diagnostics reads; only a fix changes anything. It never switches the build target and never throws.

FieldPickerModel #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Drawers · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor

public sealed class FieldPickerModel

The Field Picker of one Saveable, without any drawing: one row per field Unity serializes on each component of the GameObject, whether it can be ticked, and why not when it cannot. The Saveable's custom Inspector draws it; tests drive it directly.

Rows list the fields the Inspector shows: public or [SerializeField], not [NonSerialized], not static, not read-only, not [HideInInspector], found by reflection on the component's class and its base classes. The Transform (the Position saver covers it), the Saveable itself, scripts that implement ISaveable (they save themselves, see SelfSavingComponents) and Unity's own components (see BuiltInComponents) get no rows; only game scripts are reflected. A field of a type Shipready cannot save, or a link to a scene object that has no Saveable, is listed but greyed out, with the reason.

DemoSceneGenerator #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Generators · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor

public static class DemoSceneGenerator

Builds the four demo scenes and everything they use, in Samples/Demos: the scenes (QuickStartDemo, WorldDemo, WorldDemo_Cellar, GameUpdatesDemo, RecoveryDemo), the crate prefab and the four on-screen panel prefabs, one settings asset per demo with the demo Prefab, Asset and Scene Registries, and the version 1 example save, written through Shipready itself. Scenes, prefabs and assets are only ever generated, never hand-written YAML.

Safe to run again: every file is rebuilt in place, so GUIDs and the links between the files stay the same, and every saved object keeps a fixed id, so demo saves made before a rebuild still load. The example save is only written again when it is missing or no longer loads. Build Settings are never changed. Throws on any failure, which makes a batch-mode run exit with a non-zero code. Run it from Tools/Shipready/Generators/Rebuild Demo Scenes, which asks first, or with -executeMethod RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Generators.DemoSceneGenerator.Generate.

The demo scripts live in their own assembly, which a game may delete together with the Samples folder. So that deleting them never breaks Shipready's editor code, this generator refers to them by name and sets their fields through SerializedObject; it reports clearly when they are missing.

MenuPrefabGenerator #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Generators · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor

public static class MenuPrefabGenerator

Builds the player menu's prefabs and its default theme and text assets: SaveMenu, SlotCard and ConfirmDialog in UI/Prefabs, DefaultMenuTheme and DefaultMenuText in UI/Settings. Prefabs are only ever generated, never hand-written YAML.

Safe to run again: the three prefabs are overwritten in place, so their GUIDs, and every reference to them, stay the same. The theme and text assets are created only when they are missing and are never overwritten. Throws on any failure, which makes a batch-mode run exit with a non-zero code. Run it from Tools/Shipready/Generators/Rebuild Menu Prefabs, which asks first, or with -executeMethod RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Generators.MenuPrefabGenerator.Generate.

The prefabs reference nothing outside Assets/RareGeometry/Shipready/Save: labels keep no font, so TextMesh Pro uses its default one, and the rounded shapes are made while the game runs. TextMesh Pro's essential resources must be in the project for any text to show; the generator only checks for them and says so when they are missing.

MenuStyleWindow #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.MenuStyle · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor

public sealed class MenuStyleWindow : EditorWindow

Tools > Shipready > Menu Style: makes the save menu in the open scene look and read the way the game wants, without the Project window, a prefab or code. Pick one of six ready-made styles, change any colour, the font, sizes and shape, the layout (list or grid, which details show, where the panel sits) and every word, and see it at once in the preview. A style can be exported to a .json file and imported in another project. With no save menu in the open scene, every tab edits the project's own look and words, which the next menu added gets.

Every change goes to the game's own copy of the theme and wording in the data folder, never to Shipready's assets, so Shipready updates keep it. Each action is one undo step. The preview draws a copy of the menu in a scene of its own, so it never changes the open scene.

GamePresets #

public static class GamePresets

Settings for common kinds of game, applied in one click from the Setup Wizard's first page or the settings' Basics tab. Plan(SetupWizardModel, GamePreset) lists exactly what a preset would change before anything changes; ApplyTo(SetupWizardModel, GamePreset) writes it into a SetupWizardModel, whose Apply is one undo step.

Presets only touch slots, autosave, pictures and how compact files are. They never change the encryption passphrase or key, the save folder or the file names, so every existing save stays where it is and keeps loading.

SetupWizardModel #

class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Wizard · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor

public sealed class SetupWizardModel

Everything the Setup Wizard does, without drawing anything: the choices of each step, and one Apply per step that writes them into the project. The Setup Wizard window is a thin view over this class, and tests drive it directly.

The first Apply creates the settings asset and its three registries in DataFolder, which lies outside Shipready's own folder so that a Shipready update never overwrites them, and fills the registries. Every Apply is one undo group, so Edit > Undo takes a step back; undoing the first one deletes the asset files it created. Nothing here shows a dialog. Changes lists everything created or changed, for the Finish page.

RequiredPackages #

static class in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Setup · assembly RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Setup

public static class RequiredPackages

Tells the developer which Unity packages Shipready's save menu, editor tool windows and demos need, and how to install them: uGUI (com.unity.ugui) and TextMesh Pro, which is part of uGUI from Unity 2023.2 and the separate com.unity.textmeshpro package in Unity 2022.3. Shipready never installs, updates or removes a package itself; the developer does that in the Package Manager.

This class sits in its own small editor assembly, RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Setup, which references nothing else of Shipready and compiles only while one of those packages is missing. Until they are installed, Shipready's runtime (SaveKit) and its core editor services in RareGeometry.Shipready.Save.Editor.Core (saved ids, registry upkeep and the migration link file) compile and keep working; the save menu, the Start window, the Setup Wizard, the Save Inspector and Diagnostics windows and the demos wait, so importing Shipready never ends in compile errors.

While a package is missing, this class logs one warning per editor session (not on every script reload); it never opens a dialog by itself. Tools → Shipready → Saves → Required Packages shows the same explanation, with a button that opens the Package Manager. A player build stops with the same message, because the save menu and the demos would be missing from it. Nothing is shown in batch mode, but the build check applies there too.

Returns: A new array, empty when nothing is missing. Never null.
